text:
incidents-bot: PAGER — REGION: gcp-southamerica-santiago (southamerica1) | gpu_pool: inference-pool-2 | symptom: queue growth & autoscaler pending > 10m | error: quotaExceeded: accel_attach_denied

oncall-eng: Got the page, I'm on it. Starting triage. :mag:

sre-alyssa: I see queue ~1.2k and pending pods ~180 stuck in Pending (0/4 nodes available) with attach errors. Pulling recent autoscaler logs now.

infra-jay: Confirming: GCP API shows "quotaExceeded" for GPUs in southamerica1 under project redwood-prod. Quota usage 100% / limit 64 GPUs. Recent warm pool was 40, burst requested +80 — denied.

oncall-eng: Repro: from control plane logs: `AttachAccelerator failed: com.google.api.gax.rpc.ResourceExhaustedException: Quota exceeded for resource 'GPUS'`.

support-luis: Any customer-facing impact? We have increased error rate for hosted API routes targeting southamerica by ~18% and latency spike for chat endpoints. CS watching two customers with heavy nightly batches.

customer-success-nora: Flagging Customer A and Customer B — both reported degraded throughput. Notifying them now: "We're mitigating, may route traffic to alternate regions."

eng-runtime-max: Can we fallback model variants to CPU-safe or lower-GPU variants to reduce new capacity needs? I can push routing change to prefer redwood-medium-quant for new requests in the region.

oncall-eng: Good idea. Action 1: enable model fallback for southamerica routes (max). Doing now. Action 2: pause all non-critical batch jobs in region, infra Jay please. Action 3: open cloud support case for quota increase.

infra-jay: Batch jobs paused (kubernetes label selector `app/batch-*` scaled to 0). Reduced warm pool from 40 -> 8. Created GCP ticket #TCK-2028-459 with priority HIGH. ETA on quota bump unknown.

sre-alyssa: Kicked autoscaler policy to prefer burst in other regions for pending requests. Added cross-region reroute rule: requests originating in southamerica to be routed to eu-west1 when latency budget allows. Deploying config patch now.

incidents-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE — route-adjust v2 deployed to edge: `route-policy-southamerica-202` (fallback to eu-west1 for non-SLA-critical requests).

support-luis: CS updated customers: sending targeted note asking them to enable region fallback or accept degraded SLAs for the window.

customer-success-nora: Customers OK with reroute for now, want ETA and remediation plan. They requested to be updated every 30m.

oncall-eng: Temporary workaround recap: 1) fallback to smaller model variant (done), 2) pause batch jobs (done), 3) warm pool trimmed (done), 4) cross-region reroute deployed (done). Monitoring queue length; still slowly decreasing.

infra-jay: GCP support replied: quota increase requires internal approvals, could take 2-6 hours; suggested creating quota reservation or moving some reserved capacity — not immediate.

eng-runtime-max: Additional mitigation: enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for chat routes to cut token generation by ~20%. Rolling config to prod for southamerica only.

sre-alyssa: Queue length now 520 (was 1200). Pending pods gradually dropping. No new attach errors for 4m. Latency for rerouted requests to eu-west1 increased ~70ms median — within SLO for non-critical.

oncall-eng: Passing to next oncall + handoff notes. Please ack: I'll be handing off at +30m. If quota not increased by then, we escalate to Capacity team to carve reservation.

oncall-nextshift: Acked. I'll take ownership and keep updates to customers every 30m until resolved.

customer-success-nora: Creating a short template update for customers and sharing in #support-updates.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT NOTE — severity P1 -> open. Summary added to ticket: "southamerica1 GPU quota exhausted causing attach_denied and autoscaler stall; mitigations applied: model fallback, batch pause, warm pool trim, cross-region reroute, caching improvements; cloud support engaged (#TCK-2028-459)."

oncall-eng: Final for now — monitoring and handoff. If we see queue regrow or attach errors resume, escalate to oncall-sre and Capacity with the GCP ticket. :thumbsup:
